questions.question:
Choose the option which are antonyms (opposite of) the word used in the sentence given below:

Although her happiness was manifest in her cheerful demeanour, the hidden sorrow in her eyes revealed a deeper emotional struggle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"manifest"** means something that is clear or obvious to the eye or mind. (स्पष्ट)

 
 
• **Example: **Her joy was** manifest **in her sparkling eyes and broad smile.
 
 
 
• **"Hidden" **refers to something that is concealed or not easily noticed. (छिपा हुआ)
 
 
• **Example: **Despite his cheerful facade, his true feelings remained **hidden.**
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'manifest' **is **'hidden'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Demeanour** (व्यवहार): The outward behavior or bearing of a person.

 
 
• **Example:** His calm **demeanour** during the crisis was commendable.
 
 
 
• **Sorrow** (दुःख): A feeling of deep distress caused by loss, disappointment, or other misfortune.
 
 
• **Example:** She felt deep** sorrow** after the loss of her pet.
 
 
 
• **Happiness** (खुशी): A state of well-being and contentment.
 
 
• **Example:** His **happiness** was evident when he heard the good news.
 
 
 
• **Struggle** (संघर्ष): To make strenuous or violent efforts in the face of difficulties or opposition.
 
 
• **Example:** She had to** struggle** to finish her work on time.
 
 
 
• **Revealed** (प्रकट): To make known something that was previously secret or unknown.
 
 
• **Example:** The investigation** revealed **new evidence.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Snow was falling light when everyone was leaving church.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the adjective 'light' is incorrect.
 
• The word **'lightly'** should be used instead of **'light'** to describe the manner in which the snow was falling.
 
• Therefore, the correct form is 'lightly'.

Hence, the correct statement is **"*Snow was falling lightly__ when everyone was leaving church*."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question:

__
 
• The phrase **"plan to marrying"** is** incorrect **in English grammar.
 
• The correct form is **"plan to marry,"** which uses the **base form of the verb after "to."**
 
• In English grammar, after verbs that indicate planning or intention (such as **"plan," "intend," "want")**, use the** base form of the verb **(also known as the **infinitive form**) following** "to."**
 
 
• Example: "I **plan to travel **next year."
 
 

The correct sentence is** "*They plan to marry__ in the spring.***
